gaps.title: Automated-decision safeguards exist in law (Art. 44) but are not operational for AI-assisted document verification
gaps.finding: Law 2024/017 Art. 44 gives the data subject the right to object to any decision based exclusively on automated processing, with exceptions (informed + explicit consent; authorised by law with safeguards) and the rights to obtain human intervention, to express a point of view and to contest the decision. What is NOT defined anywhere we could read: (a) whether an INCONSISTENT/INSUFFICIENT verdict used by an employer or ministry is a 'decision'; (b) who is the controller of an AI verdict (verifier, registrar, issuing university); (c) whether human review is proactive or only on request; (d) any duty to explain which evidence drove the verdict. There is no AI statute or AI authority yet (SNIA, as reported, announces a framework law).
gaps.correction: The first seed said Law 2024/017 'reportedly does not address automated decision-making'. The primary text (OCR of the Presidency's certified copy) contains Art. 44, so the gap is operational detail, not total absence.

law_cited.note: right to object to exclusively automated decisions; exceptions
human intervention, point of view, contest
AI Authority, Presidential Council on AI and framework law announced, not yet enacted

gaps.proposal: Make human review of every adverse or uncertain AI verdict mandatory and proactive for employment/admission uses, with a written explanation of the evidence used (rules PR-REGISTRAR-001, PR-HUMAN-REVIEW-001, both proposal: true); define the registrar as the accountable person.
gaps.comparison: EU: GDPR Art. 22 and AI Act Art. 14 (human oversight) and Art. 86 (right to explanation; education systems are high-risk, Annex III) — comparison only, not binding in Cameroon. AU Malabo Convention Art. 14 states the same 'no decision based solely on automated processing' principle (Cameroon's ratification NOT verified).
gaps.verification: Art. 44 read in the OCR text (primary). SNIA content as reported by OECD.AI / Business in Cameroon (secondary).

gaps.title: Probative value of online verification results and of digitised/OCR copies of archives is undefined
gaps.finding: Law 2024/001 Art. 29 gives a certified copy produced by the national archive body the same evidential admission as the original; Art. 19(2) leaves the management/conservation of electronic archives to future regulation; Law 2010/021 Art. 13 allows an electronic writing under Civil Code conditions; Law 2010/012 declares a 'legal regime of digital evidence' (Section 1). None of these texts addresses (i) a scan/OCR copy held by a university or exam board, (ii) the output of an automated verification platform or of a tool such as VeriDiplo, (iii) hashing / chain of custody of an evidence pack.

law_cited.note: certified copy = original, only when produced by the national archive body

gaps.proposal: MINESUP and the archive body define the evidential status of digitised copies and verification results, mandatory hashing and chain-of-custody metadata (PROV-O), and which institution may certify an evidence pack.
gaps.comparison: UAE: verification is performed by officially appointed agencies (Dataflow, QuadraBay) that contact the issuing university directly and issue a final report through the ministry portal (The National, 2025, as reported) — evidential value attaches to the agency/ministry report, not to the document copy.
gaps.verification: Articles read in the downloaded texts; absence of other provisions = 'not found in the texts reviewed', not proof of absence.

gaps.title: No published retention schedule for verification requests and uploaded diplomas
gaps.finding: Law 2024/017 Art. 13 forbids keeping data longer than necessary and says the period is stated in the processing authorisation; Art. 28 says the maximum period is set in the Authority's reference framework (référentiel, Art. 27). We found no such schedule published, and the Authority's operational status is reported as uncertain (see P4).

law_cited.note: no longer than necessary; period fixed in authorisation / by regulation
maximum period set in the Authority's référentiel

gaps.proposal: Default 90 days then deletion of uploads (OUR proposal, not law); keep only the hashed audit record. To be replaced by the Authority's schedule once published.
gaps.verification: Articles read (OCR). Non-existence of a schedule is 'not found', to confirm with the Authority.

gaps.title: Cross-border academic verification depends on a prior authorisation regime that cannot yet be exercised
gaps.finding: Law 2024/017 Art. 32 subordinates any transfer of personal data to a foreign State or international organisation to the prior authorisation of the Authority, checking adequate protection, a signed legal instrument with the destination country, binding security rules and Authority-published standard contractual clauses. Art. 53 gives the Authority the task of publishing the list of countries recognised as adequate. Secondary sources consulted 10 Nov 2026 report that implementing decrees / the Authority's operation were still pending (as reported, to verify) and that the law applies after an 18-month transition (23 June 2026). We found no published adequacy list, no standard clauses and no simplified route for a yes/no attestation. Cloud-LLM calls (S4/LLM provider) are transfers too.

law_cited.note: Authority issues authorisations and publishes the list of adequate countries

gaps.proposal: Simplified regime for minimal yes/no attestations (+ hash, no personal data beyond the holder's own claim) with a transfer log; until the Authority issues authorisations, only such attestations leave Cameroon (rules PR-CROSSBORDER-001/002).
gaps.comparison: UAE: federal PDPL 45/2021 sets requirements for cross-border transfer (u.ae overview, summary); degree verification is delegated to two appointed agencies with UAE PASS login and a ministry-issued report; MoHRE launched a digital employer verification service (Gulf News, May 2025, as reported). AU Malabo Art. 14 and ECOWAS Supplementary Act give an adequacy-based model (not binding on Cameroon).
gaps.verification: Art. 32/53 read (OCR). Authority status and 18-month transition = secondary sources (as_reported).

gaps.title: Holder consent is required for MINESUP equivalence/authentication, but no general rule governs employer-initiated checks or bulk queries
gaps.finding: The MINESUP equivalence form carries an 'Autorisation de recherche d'informations' by which the holder authorises the Minister to carry out the searches needed to authenticate the diploma. Law 2024/017 Art. 9 requires prior, free, informed, specific and unambiguous consent, with derogations (legal obligation, public-interest mission, vital interests) that leave open whether an employer's 'legitimate interest' qualifies; Art. 50 prohibits processing without consent. Nothing limits the number of holders an HR firm can check, and no consent format (paper form only) exists for digital checks.

law_cited.note: holder authorisation to the Minister only

gaps.proposal: A consent token or an explicit statutory legal basis for every check; legal basis accepted only from public authorities; rate limit per verifier (20 holders/hour, our proposal).
gaps.comparison: UAE: employer verification goes through the ministry platform / appointed agencies; the holder logs in with UAE PASS (as reported).
gaps.verification: Form and Art. 9/50 read in the downloaded texts.

gaps.title: Liability and wording for AI false positives are undefined; outputs may pre-empt a criminal qualification
gaps.finding: Art. 62 of Law 2024/017 gives the data subject urgent judicial measures and a claim for reparation, but no text allocates liability between verifier, registrar, tool provider and issuing institution when an automated INCONSISTENT verdict is wrong. The Penal Code defines forgery (Art. 144, 314-315) and unlawful use of an official diploma (Art. 219) as offences for courts to establish; no text regulates how verification tools may word their findings. The stakes are real: press reports ~1,000 gendarmerie trainees dismissed in 2022 and 1,312 diplomas reported as fake in June 2024 (as reported).

law_cited.note: unlawful use of an official diploma

gaps.proposal: Shared-accountability clause (registrar approves, tool provider logs, verifier acts only on approved verdicts); never output 'fake'; hash-chained audit log as evidence of who decided what.
gaps.comparison: UAE: findings are 'authenticated or not' reports issued by the ministry after the agency contacts the university (as reported); no automated accusation.
gaps.verification: Articles read in downloaded texts; dismissal figures from press (as_reported).

gaps.title: No published legal basis, access conditions or holder rights for the national online diploma-verification platform
gaps.finding: Press (as reported) says the government platform launched on 1 Oct 2024 (MINESUP/MINFOPRA) rests on an agreement of 6 Apr 2023 and a joint circular of 8 May 2024 under which MINESUP gives MINFOPRA a secure software interface to diploma data, to be extended to MINESEC, MINEDUB and MINEFOP. We found no published text on who may query it (private employers?), on logging, on holder notification or on rectification, nor on interoperability with third-party tools.
gaps.proposal: Publish the circular and an access policy (who, purpose, logging, holder notice, SLA) and an open API/credential format so that third-party tools such as VeriDiplo can federate instead of duplicating.
gaps.comparison: UAE: ministries publish the attestation/verification workflow and fees online (The National, MoE news, as reported).
gaps.verification: Press only (kind: summary, as_reported). The circular itself was not obtained.

gaps.title: Text of the 2023 higher-education orientation law (and any diploma-authentication decree) could not be obtained
gaps.finding: Law 2023/007 of 25 July 2023 (reported to have 117 articles and to repeal Law 2001/005) is not available as a public PDF we could reach; the repealed 2001 law is in the KB for historical context only. We therefore cannot say whether the current law assigns diploma registry, authentication or archive duties, nor which arrêté governs the authentication procedure.
gaps.proposal: Publish the law and its implementing texts in the Journal officiel/PRC site in a machine-readable form; the human team must drop the PDF in kb/raw/CM-HE-2023.pdf and re-run the build.
gaps.verification: Documentation gap of this KB, honestly flagged.

gaps.title: No deadline or structured-format duty for institutions to answer verification requests or export deliberation registers
gaps.finding: Law 2024/001 Art. 30(3) requires reasoned refusals of archive communication and Art. 19(2) defers electronic-archive modalities to regulation, but we found no deadline for issuers (universities, Office du Baccalauréat, GCE Board) to confirm a diploma, and no duty to hold deliberation minutes (PV) as structured/digitised records. Missing or unreadable archives (S5) therefore end in 'insufficient evidence' with no escalation path.

law_cited.note: evidence by certified copies from the national archive body

gaps.proposal: Response deadline for issuers, mandatory digitised + structured result registers, and an archive-request template (the system drafts it in S5).
gaps.comparison: UAE: the agency contacts the university and the duration depends on the university's response (The National, as reported) — same bottleneck, partially managed by SLAs on the agency side.
gaps.verification: Articles read; absence of a deadline = not found in texts reviewed.

gaps.title: Binding status for Cameroon of the African recognition and data-protection conventions is not established
gaps.finding: The Addis Ababa revised recognition convention (Art. IV.2(3): Parties commit to eradicate fraudulent practices regarding qualifications; network exchange of counter-fraud measures) is binding only on Parties. The UN registration record in the KB lists 12 Parties and Cameroon is not among them (it appears on the signature pages). Cameroon's ratification of the AU Malabo Convention was not verified.
evidence: source INT-ADDIS-2014 (OCR of UN record, pages 1-2 and 12-22)
gaps.proposal: Confirm status with UNESCO/AU; if Cameroon is not a Party, ratify/accede so that cross-border verification and counter-fraud cooperation have a treaty basis.
gaps.comparison: Global Convention (UNESCO 2019) and Lisbon Convention not downloaded (pending) — compare once available.
gaps.verification: Party list read in OCR of the UN record (dated registration 2020; may be outdated).

gaps.title: No reconciliation procedure for name variants and OCR/transcription errors between civil status, diplomas and deliberation minutes
gaps.finding: Law 2024/017 Art. 12 requires accurate, up-to-date data and a duty to correct inaccurate data, and the rights chapter lets the holder obtain rectification; nothing describes how a holder whose compound name, name order or spelling differs across civil-status documents, diplomas and PVs obtains a documented reconciliation, nor what a verifier may do meanwhile.
gaps.proposal: Fuzzy-match results between 80 and 92 are 'unknown' and go to human review with a rectification path offered to the holder (rules PR-HUMAN-REVIEW-001, PR-HOLDER-NOTICE-001).
gaps.comparison: UAE: a mandatory 'name change document' (legal letter, birth/marriage certificate or earlier passport) is required when the certificate name differs from the passport (The National, as reported).

gaps.title: No AI statute, AI authority or regulatory-sandbox regime yet: pilots like this one have no legal status
gaps.finding: SNIA (July 2025, as reported by OECD.AI) plans a Cameroonian AI Authority, a Presidential Council on AI and a framework law; none was found enacted. Without a sandbox regime there is no framework that tells a pilot what data it may use, who supervises it, or when it may go live.

law_cited.note: authority, council and framework law announced

evidence: all scenarios run in the sandbox profile
readiness dimension 10 (AI & Policies), metric d10_m01 Policy Sandbox
gaps.proposal: A policy-sandbox decree defining admissible synthetic/real data, supervisor, exit criteria and publication of sandbox findings (policy case briefs, d10_m08).
gaps.comparison: Not compared (no regulatory-sandbox text in the KB).

gaps.title: No national machine-readable schema for diploma / deliberation-minutes (PV) data
gaps.finding: No Cameroonian or African schema for diplomas, PV rows, registers or accreditation periods was found; each institution uses its own layout.
gaps.proposal: Contribute the VeriDiplo ontology; align credentials with W3C VC 2.0 and provenance with PROV-O.
gaps.comparison: W3C VC Data Model 2.0 (issuer, credentialSubject, evidence) is the generic building block; no education profile for Cameroon.

gaps.title: No standard format for policy-as-code linked to legal provisions
gaps.finding: Rules cite legal text only in prose. VeriDiplo links each rule to chunk ids/anchors of a machine-readable KB and tags proposals vs law.
gaps.proposal: Propose the YAML rule schema + context contract (kb/policy_rules/context_schema.yaml) and chunk/anchor format to ITU study groups.
gaps.comparison: OECD/NIST/ISO 42001 describe governance processes, not an executable rule format (ISO text not accessible: pending).

gaps.title: ITU-T Y.3172 has no provenance/evidence node, no human-approval gate and a minimal security clause; its P node acts only on model output
gaps.finding: Y.3172 clause 8.1 defines P as the node that 'enables the application of policies to the output of the model node' (example: network-safety rules). It sits between M and D, so it cannot govern ingestion (SRC/C), search, or export decisions, carries no consent/purpose concept, no human approval of an output, no provenance/evidence record and no explainability requirement. Clause 9 (security) is two sentences (authentication/authorisation, prevent unauthorised access and data leaking). The Recommendation targets ML in IMT-2020 networks; applying it to document verification is our adaptation.
gaps.proposal: Add to Y.3172 a P-node sub-function 'evidence and approval gate' (checkpoints before ingest/search/report/share/export, human approval, audit hash chain) and a provenance requirement on C/PP.
gaps.comparison: EU AI Act Art. 12 (record-keeping), 14 (human oversight) cover what Y.3172 lacks, for AI systems in general.

gaps.title: No OCR benchmark for French/English Cameroonian administrative scans and names
gaps.finding: The KB itself needed a custom binarisation step to OCR the watermarked certified copy of Law 2024/017 reliably (default OCR garbled several articles).
gaps.proposal: Release the synthetic benchmark (degraded PV scans, compound names, both name orders) openly.

gaps.title: No standard for digital consent evidence (consent token) in education-credential verification
gaps.finding: Art. 9 requires consent that is prior, free, informed, specific and unambiguous but the only artefact found is a paper authorisation (MINESUP form).
gaps.proposal: A signed, purpose-bound, expiring consent credential (W3C VC 2.0 profile) verified by the Policy Guardian.
gaps.comparison: UAE: UAE PASS login of the holder on the agency portal (as reported).

gaps.title: AI Readiness 2.0 has no metric for multi-agent coordination, human approval gates or evidence-pack integrity
gaps.finding: Readiness 2.0 (13 dimensions, machine-readable in kb/framework/dimensions.json) contains related metrics — d8_m01 'Co-creation Ease (human in inference process)', d10_m07 'Explainability Metrics', d10_m09 'Audit Metrics', d6_m06 'Safety Integration' — but none measures coordination of several agents under a policy guardian, the rate of human-approved vs auto-released adverse outputs, or integrity/provenance of evidence.
gaps.proposal: Add metrics: human-gate coverage (% adverse outputs human-approved), audit-chain verifiability, proposal-vs-law rule ratio, evidence-linked-output ratio.

gaps.title: No interoperable format for cross-border verification results (yes/no attestation + hash)
gaps.finding: Verification results are currently reports on national portals/agency accounts; no portable, minimal, verifiable result format was found. The Addis Convention foresees an African network exchanging counter-fraud information but gives no technical format.
gaps.proposal: Define a minimal verification-attestation credential (verdict class, institution, session, record hash, issuer signature) as a W3C VC 2.0 profile for AU/ECOWAS/CEMAC use.
gaps.comparison: UAE agencies deliver proprietary PDF reports via UAE PASS portals (as reported).

gaps.title: No shared vocabulary for verification outcomes (consistent / inconsistent / insufficient evidence) or for non-accusatory wording
gaps.finding: W3C VC 2.0 offers an 'evidence' property (section 5.6) for supporting information but no outcome vocabulary; national platforms report 'authentic or not' (as reported).

law_cited.note: related section; the 'evidence' property is section 5.6

gaps.proposal: Standardise a three-state verdict with mandatory evidence references and a neutral wording list; publish it with the KB format.
gaps.comparison: UAE reports a binary authenticated / not authenticated result (as reported).
